explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/20, which quotes Erdős–Rado as f(n,k) ≤ (k−1)^n n!. The Lean form is f(n,k) ≤ (k−1)^n n! + 1, which is the precise bound: a family with more than (k−1)^n n! members contains a sunflower, and the (k−1)^n n! extremal family has none in the classical example for n = 1. So the +1 follows the definition of f here, while the page's phrasing is loose. The restriction k ≥ 2 avoids truncated subtraction. Faithful.
